summary: James Matthew Baskind is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

James McHugh specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), working under Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He has held posts at Cornell and the University of Southern California.

James Miller is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Cambridge (1997) and a PhD from Boston University (2000). He was attested as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast in 2014.
James Morison was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as a librarian at the University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Murdoch was a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Aberdeen and under Theodor Benfey (~1878–1880). He held posts at Kanazawa University (~1898–1900), Kagoshima University (~1901–1908), and the University of Tokyo.

James Prinsep was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served at the Benares Mint (~1820–1830), the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1819, 1830–1838), and led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), where he founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

James R. Ballantyne was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He taught at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy (1832–1845), served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1845–1861), and was librarian at the India Office.

James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned his PhD from Stanford. He taught at Williams College and the University of Michigan, and has held professorships and directorships at Harvard University, including the Harvard-Yenching Institute (2024).

James Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served at California State University (attested 1998) and as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).

James Smith Reid was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1865–1869). He held posts at Christ's College (1869–1880), Pembroke College (1873–1885), and Gonville and Caius College (1878–1926).

James Sutherland Cotton was an Indologist and historian who studied at Trinity College, Oxford (1867–1870). He held posts at The Queen's College, Oxford (1871–1874) and Queens' College, Cambridge (1871–1874).

James Tod was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich, and under Gyanchandra. He served in the East India Company (~1799–1823) and as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).
James W. Benson is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts as Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

James W. Heisig is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge and served as a Permanent Research Fellow at Nanzan University across multiple periods between 1976 and 2001.
James Ward was a philosopher who studied at Fitzwilliam College and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~1897 to 1925.
James Whitehill is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000) and founded the Columbia Zen Center.

James Wilson Bright was a linguist who earned his PhD from Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882) and taught at Cornell (~1885). He served as the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins from 1905 to 1925.

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, and Patrul Rinpoche, and taught numerous students, including Shechen Gyaltsab and Khenpo Shenga.

3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche (1973), Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Thegchog Dorje, and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa, both of whom he also taught.
